## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8')) if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim() const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.') mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true }) const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) } let browser try { browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient) for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) { const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient) page.setDefaultTimeout(30000) const failures = [] page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) }) page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) }) const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient) if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 }) await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' }) await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded') const start = await startForCapture(page, { enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false', selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || '' }) console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`) await page.waitForTimeout(1000) await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => { if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error) throw error }) if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`) await page.close() } } catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 } finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project.

// Tiny procedural sound engine — no external assets required.
export class SoundEngine {
  constructor() {
    this.ctx = null
    this.master = null
    this.muted = false
    this.ambient = null
    this.night = false
  }

  init() {
    if (this.ctx) return
    const AC = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext
    if (!AC) return
    this.ctx = new AC()
    this.master = this.ctx.createGain()
    this.master.gain.value = 0.55
    this.master.connect(this.ctx.destination)
    this.noiseBuffer = this.makeNoise()
    this.startAmbient()
  }

  resume() { this.ctx?.resume?.() }

  makeNoise() {
    const len = this.ctx.sampleRate * 2
    const buf = this.ctx.createBuffer(1, len, this.ctx.sampleRate)
    const data = buf.getChannelData(0)
    for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1
    return buf
  }

  setMuted(muted) {
    this.muted = muted
    if (this.master) this.master.gain.setTargetAtTime(muted ? 0 : 0.55, this.ctx.currentTime, 0.08)
  }

  tone({ freq = 440, to = freq, dur = 0.15, type = 'sine', vol = 0.2, delay = 0, attack = 0.01 }) {
    if (!this.ctx || this.muted) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime + delay
    const osc = this.ctx.createOscillator()
    const gain = this.ctx.createGain()
    osc.type = type
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, t)
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(20, to), t + dur)
    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)
    gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(vol, t + attack)
    gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + dur)
    osc.connect(gain).connect(this.master)
    osc.start(t); osc.stop(t + dur + 0.03)
  }

  noise({ dur = 0.3, vol = 0.15, filter = 900, to = filter, delay = 0, q = 0.8 }) {
    if (!this.ctx || this.muted) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime + delay
    const src = this.ctx.createBufferSource()
    src.buffer = this.noiseBuffer
    const f = this.ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    f.type = 'bandpass'; f.Q.value = q
    f.frequency.setValueAtTime(filter, t)
    f.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(60, to), t + dur)
    const gain = this.ctx.createGain()
    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(vol, t)
    gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + dur)
    src.connect(f).connect(gain).connect(this.master)
    src.start(t); src.stop(t + dur + 0.03)
  }

  startAmbient() {
    if (!this.ctx) return
    const c = this.ctx
    const out = c.createGain(); out.gain.value = 0.075; out.connect(this.master)
    const a = c.createOscillator(); a.type = 'sine'; a.frequency.value = 48
    const b = c.createOscillator(); b.type = 'triangle'; b.frequency.value = 55.7
    const filter = c.createBiquadFilter(); filter.type = 'lowpass'; filter.frequency.value = 180
    const lfo = c.createOscillator(); lfo.frequency.value = 0.07
    const lfoGain = c.createGain(); lfoGain.gain.value = 18
    lfo.connect(lfoGain).connect(filter.frequency)
    a.connect(filter); b.connect(filter); filter.connect(out)
    a.start(); b.start(); lfo.start()
    this.ambient = { out, filter }
  }

  setNight(night) {
    if (!this.ambient || this.night === night) return
    this.night = night
    this.ambient.out.gain.setTargetAtTime(night ? 0.1 : 0.065, this.ctx.currentTime, 1.5)
    this.ambient.filter.frequency.setTargetAtTime(night ? 130 : 210, this.ctx.currentTime, 1.5)
  }

  play(name) {
    if (!this.ctx || this.muted) return
    switch (name) {
      case 'click': this.tone({ freq: 620, to: 520, dur: 0.06, type: 'triangle', vol: 0.07 }); break
      case 'cast':
        this.noise({ dur: 0.4, vol: 0.12, filter: 2400, to: 300, q: 1.2 })
        this.tone({ freq: 300, to: 700, dur: 0.25, type: 'sine', vol: 0.06 })
        break
      case 'splash':
        this.noise({ dur: 0.5, vol: 0.13, filter: 900, to: 120, q: 0.6 })
        this.tone({ freq: 120, to: 48, dur: 0.4, type: 'sine', vol: 0.16 })
        break
      case 'bite':
        this.tone({ freq: 880, to: 660, dur: 0.1, type: 'square', vol: 0.08 })
        this.tone({ freq: 1180, to: 980, dur: 0.14, type: 'triangle', vol: 0.09, delay: 0.11 })
        break
      case 'reel':
        this.tone({ freq: 220, to: 760, dur: 0.5, type: 'sawtooth', vol: 0.06 })
        this.noise({ dur: 0.4, vol: 0.08, filter: 1200, to: 400 })
        break
      case 'chest':
        [523, 659, 784, 1046].forEach((f, i) => this.tone({ freq: f, dur: 0.5, type: 'triangle', vol: 0.1, delay: i * 0.09 }))
        this.tone({ freq: 130, to: 260, dur: 0.3, type: 'sine', vol: 0.12 })
        break
      case 'pickup':
        this.tone({ freq: 720, to: 1080, dur: 0.12, type: 'sine', vol: 0.07 })
        break
      case 'chop':
        this.noise({ dur: 0.18, vol: 0.2, filter: 800, to: 180, q: 0.7 })
        this.tone({ freq: 160, to: 70, dur: 0.18, type: 'square', vol: 0.09 })
        break
      case 'hit':
        this.noise({ dur: 0.2, vol: 0.16, filter: 1500, to: 200 })
        this.tone({ freq: 190, to: 80, dur: 0.2, type: 'sawtooth', vol: 0.07 })
        break
      case 'hurt':
        this.tone({ freq: 210, to: 90, dur: 0.35, type: 'sawtooth', vol: 0.12 })
        this.noise({ dur: 0.25, vol: 0.1, filter: 500, to: 150 })
        break
      case 'monster':
        this.tone({ freq: 90, to: 42, dur: 0.8, type: 'sawtooth', vol: 0.1 })
        this.noise({ dur: 0.7, vol: 0.07, filter: 260, to: 90 })
        break
      case 'boss':
        this.tone({ freq: 55, to: 28, dur: 2.2, type: 'sawtooth', vol: 0.2 })
        this.noise({ dur: 2, vol: 0.12, filter: 300, to: 60, q: 0.4 })
        break
      case 'craft':
        [392, 523, 659].forEach((f, i) => this.tone({ freq: f, dur: 0.22, type: 'triangle', vol: 0.07, delay: i * 0.07 }))
        break
      case 'place':
        this.tone({ freq: 150, to: 90, dur: 0.2, type: 'sine', vol: 0.12 })
        this.noise({ dur: 0.2, vol: 0.06, filter: 400 })
        break
      case 'eat': this.noise({ dur: 0.15, vol: 0.08, filter: 700, to: 300 }); break
      case 'drink': this.tone({ freq: 300, to: 500, dur: 0.18, type: 'sine', vol: 0.06 }); break
      case 'error': this.tone({ freq: 160, to: 120, dur: 0.16, type: 'square', vol: 0.05 }); break
      case 'night':
        this.tone({ freq: 220, to: 110, dur: 2.2, type: 'sine', vol: 0.07 })
        this.tone({ freq: 330, to: 165, dur: 2.6, type: 'triangle', vol: 0.04, delay: 0.3 })
        break
      case 'dawn':
        [330, 440, 550, 660].forEach((f, i) => this.tone({ freq: f, dur: 1.1, type: 'sine', vol: 0.05, delay: i * 0.18 }))
        break
      case 'level':
        [523, 659, 880, 1318].forEach((f, i) => this.tone({ freq: f, dur: 0.7, type: 'triangle', vol: 0.08, delay: i * 0.1 }))
        break
      case 'victory':
        [392, 523, 659, 784, 1046].forEach((f, i) => this.tone({ freq: f, dur: 1.6, type: 'sine', vol: 0.1, delay: i * 0.18 }))
        break
      case 'trial':
        this.tone({ freq: 65, to: 55, dur: 3, type: 'sawtooth', vol: 0.16 })
        this.noise({ dur: 3, vol: 0.09, filter: 420, to: 80, q: 0.5 })
        break
    }
  }
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person survival game for phone/tablet from the saved issue #4 prompt: wake on a 3×3 plot in a black void, fish chests from the void with a rod, collect food/water/gear/materials/land plots, manage a 10-slot backpack (expands at levels 10, 20, …), expand the island, survive until a 7-day grace period ends, then fight monsters.

## Requirements
- First-person 3D survival game; responsive Android/iOS phone/tablet support with usable touch controls and safe areas.
- 3×3 starting plot surrounded only by black void; nothing on the plot except the starting fishing rod.
- Fishing rod casts into the void to obtain chests containing food, water, axe, weapons, materials, and plot deeds.
- Real-time survival; day/night cycle; monsters barred until the beginning phase (“week”) wears off.
- Backpack starts at 10 slots, expands at level 10 and each +10 levels.
- Build request: no clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (≤1280px wide) and read only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Tech stack: Vite + Three.js, no external art assets; all models/textures/sounds procedural.
- Interpreted “real time” as continuous live survival/day cycle; 1 in-game day = 180 real seconds.
- Seven-day grace: trial begins on dawn of day 8 (`TRIAL_DAY = 8` internally), HUD shows days 1–7 of grace.
- Added campfire resting to advance a day so the trial is reachable in a normal session; sleeping is disabled during the trial.
- Added a boss (“The Hollow Herald”) at trial start to provide a concrete win condition.
- Trial starts automatically after ~48 seconds of active trial time; waves spawn beforehand.
- Implemented early pity loot so the first five successful catches guarantee axe, sapling, deed, spear, etc.
- Uses emoji-free inline SVG item icons for consistent rendering.
- Pointer lock supported on desktop; drag-look fallback; touch joystick + drag-look; action button is contextual (cast/reel/chop/rest/collect/strike/place).

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person survival game for phone/tablet from the saved issue #4 prompt: wake on a 3×3 plot in a black void, fish chests from the void with a rod, gather food/water/gear/materials/land, manage a 10-slot backpack, expand the island, survive a 7-day grace period, then fight monsters.

## Requirements
- First-person 3D survival game with responsive Android/iOS phone and tablet support, usable touch controls, and safe-area handling.
- Starting plot is 3×3 surrounded only by black void; nothing on it except the starting fishing rod.
- Fishing rod casts into the void to obtain chests containing food, water, axe, weapons, materials, and plot deeds.
- Real-time survival with day/night cycle; monsters barred until the grace period ends.
- Backpack starts at 10 slots and expands at level 10 and each +10 levels.
- Build request: no clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (≤1280px wide) and read only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Tech stack: Vite + Three.js; all models, textures, and sounds are procedural with no external art assets.
- “Real time” is continuous live survival/day cycle; 1 in-game day = 180 real seconds.
- Seven-day grace period ends on day 8 (`TRIAL_DAY = 8`); HUD shows days 1–7 remaining.
- Campfire resting advances a day so the trial is reachable in a normal session; sleeping is disabled during the trial.
- Added a boss, “The Hollow Herald,” at trial start to provide a concrete win condition; boss appears after ~48s of trial time.
- Early pity loot guarantees axe, sapling, deed, spear, etc. across the first five catches.
- FIFA-style inline SVG item icons are used instead of emoji.
- Desktop pointer lock works; drag-look fallback exists. Touch uses joystick + drag-look; action button is contextual (cast/reel/chop/rest/collect/strike/place).
- A QA harness is exposed only with `?debug=1` as `window.__VOIDLINE__`.
- Rod/tool models were rebuilt to project forward from the fist rather than lying across the screen.
- The Hollow Herald uses scale 1.5, a visible face/core, and no duplicate 3D boss health bar (HUD bar handles it).

## Work State
### Completed
- Full production build works (`npm run build`) and serves via the running watch build on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Core gameplay implemented: first-person movement/collision, camera, touch controls, pointer lock/drag look, procedural 3×3 island, void shader, stars, sky, day/night lighting, floating rocks and grass.
- Fishing state machine, early/random loot tables, pity drops, chest rise/open, loot overlay.
- Inventory, stacking, capacity scaling, item use/equip/drop, hotbar.
- Tree planting/growth/chopping, campfire, condensation still, land-deed placement with ghost tiles.
- Fabricator recipes, survival stats, death/respawn, XP/levels, auto-save/load.
- Trial waves, monster AI/combat, boss fight, victory overlay, Herald Core.
- HUD, objectives, banners, toasts, death/victory panels, settings/mute, responsive CSS.
- Start screen with cinematic camera and saved-session continue button.
- Full gameplay Playwright flow passes: catch axe → catch sapling → plant → catch deed → wait 45s growth → chop tree → expand plot → craft campfire → rest 7 times → trial active; no console errors. Log: `/tmp/opencode/test-gameplay.log`.
- Debug flow passes: boss bar visible, boss defeat triggers victory overlay and adds Herald Core, death overlay works after resetting `postGame`; no console errors.
- Visual fixes: rod is attached to hand with tapered shaft, small reel, glow bands; axe/spear/blade rebuilt; island rim dimmed; ghost tiles flattened/softened; campfire smaller/orange with reduced light; Hollow Herald redesigned with mantle, collar, horns, three eyes, glowing chest core.
- Fixed casting being blocked by a growing sapling or charging still via directional `facingAmount`/`inReach` filtering in `nearby()`.
- Fixed hotbar showing the axe icon before the axe is owned.
- Fixed boss flash-resize bug and hidden the duplicate 3D boss health bar.
- Added mobile trial rule hiding the objective panel while `body.trial-active`.
- Restored the joystick in landscape; moved vitals above it.
- Platform-aware hint text: desktop shows `Space`/`B`; touch instructions differ.
- Wording corrected to “seven days then trial” / day 8, and trial banner now says `GRACE ENDED`.
- Rest banner now shows the new day and does not overwrite the trial-start banner.

### Active
- Mobile portrait layout verification and fixes from screenshots `20-mobile-start.jpg`–`24-mobile-landscape.jpg`.
- Mobile portrait currently has joystick/hotbar overlap: joystick still at bottom `14px`; move it to about `bottom: calc(78px + safe)` in the `max-width: 720px` block.
- Mobile brand name overlaps the centered trial pill; hide `.brand-name` or otherwise reflow the topbar below 500px.
- Held rod/hand is not visible in portrait because the camera’s narrow horizontal FOV crops it; adapt hand position by aspect ratio (e.g., portrait `x≈0.22`, `y≈-0.36`, scale `≈0.9`).
- Mobile inventory panel was measured at `x=30, width=390` after 500ms, likely mid-slide-in animation; re-check after a longer wait and confirm the close button fits.
- Mobile start controls row shows confusing “move / mouse / drag” with keyboard labels hidden; hide the row on coarse pointers or replace with touch instructions.
- Need to inspect `22-mobile-cast.jpg`, `23-mobile-inventory.jpg`, `24-mobile-landscape.jpg` for other overlaps.
- Final rebuild and fresh desktop/mobile captures still pending.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. In `src/style.css` `@media (max-width: 720px)`, move `.joystick` to `bottom: calc(78px + var(--safe-b))`; re-run `/tmp/opencode/test-mobile.mjs` with longer waits before measuring the inventory panel.
